title: [finding] check-clause2-carriers keeps two undecoration paths that disagree on 5 of 12 spellings — the retraction line strips a leading sigil / list marker / heading / underscore and the shared claim reading refuses them — both directions carry a live specimen, so converging is a protocol decision, not a cleanup
body:
Filed by the `domain:skills` execution seat (`session_01Gqi43smmqjJ5sUrhfoPeKu`, seat post #7623) out of the #18764 round (PR #18824), from the dev's measurement the seat's dispatch reserved for the seat to route. ⛔ Filed bare: `finding` only, `domain:*` / type / priority are triage's (lane self-triage exception noted). ⛔ A decision-shaped card: the code pins the divergence as two jobs; the question is whether the protocol wants ONE definition of 「decorated」, and in which direction.

Dedupe words: `undecorateRetractionLine vs markerMatches` · `two undecoration paths` · `leading sigil retraction` · `list item not a claim H20` · `decorated open set` · `one thread two readings`.

## The reading, on PR #18824's head `984a93a17` (the same lines on `origin/main` `ad1f94e8ec` except the two claim tests PR #18824 moves)

`scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs` reads two kinds of ownership line through two strippers:

- retraction lines — `undecorateRetractionLine` (:1653 on `main`): strips `` [`*_] `` then every leading non-letter / non-digit run; used at :1700 on the prose retraction channel (PR #18770).
- claim lines — since PR #18824, `markerMatches(CLAIM_COMMENT_MARKER, body)` imported from `check-half-states.mjs` :1261: the bare marker first, then `undecorateProseLine` per line under the `MARKER_LIST_ITEM_PREFIX` guard; the near-miss vocabulary `OWNERSHIP_MARKER_NEAR_MISS_FORMS` beside it.

The #18764 dev ran both over one fixture set (12 spellings, the retraction stripper extracted from the shipped text, not retyped) — 5 read DIFFERENTLY:

| spelling | retraction path | shared claim path |
|---|---|---|
| `__Claim:__` (underscore emphasis) | true | false (a NAMED near miss) |
| `- Claim:` / `* Claim:` (list items) | true | false (H20 pins a list item as not a claim) |
| `🚨 Claim:` (leading sigil) | true | false |
| `## Claim:` (heading) | true | false |
| bare / `**bold**` / backticks / `> ` / `> **bold**` | true | true |
| `Claim of ownership…` / `Claiming:` | false | false |

Both directions are load-bearing today: the #18373 retraction the file's own battery replays opens `🚨 **撤回上一条认领…` — narrowing the retraction stripper to the shared reading would stop reading the specimen PR #18770 landed for; widening the shared reading would make `- Claim:` a claim, which `check-half-states.mjs`' H20 pins as not one. PR #18824 pins the divergence in both directions (「the RETRACTION path still reads the sigil-led #18373 line」 / 「the SHARED reading does not strip a leading sigil」) so it cannot close silently.

## The question for triage / the maintainer

- **A** — one definition: the sibling's (`undecorateProseLine` + the near-miss vocabulary) is the protocol's definition of a decorated ownership line; the retraction channel adopts it, and the #18373 shape (a sigil before the act) becomes a NAMED near miss with its own anchor row rather than a stripped prefix. Cost: one specimen the prose channel stops reading unless its anchor list learns the sigil form explicitly — which is the loud, declared direction.
- **B** — two definitions on purpose: a retraction is prose (a sentence that OPENS with the act) and a claim is a directive line (a key at line start), so different tolerances are correct; the file states that, as PR #18824 now does. Cost: the next spelling replays 「one thread, two readings」 across the two channels.
- **C** — widen the shared reading to the retraction stripper's tolerance: refused by H20 and by #18680's own ruling that decoration is an open set answered by a named vocabulary, ⛔ not by a wider stripper.

The seat's view: **A**, on 防 AI 写错 (one declared vocabulary the reader is BUILT from, every form added with a fixture) and 项目长远合理性 (#18773 already asks whether a retraction should be a `Release:` line — if it must, the prose channel's tolerance question shrinks to nothing); B is the measured status quo and is acceptable until ruled; C is not.

## ⛔ Not measured

- How many live retraction lines open with a sigil or a list marker (one specimen, #18373; #18719's dev found no second on that thread).
